$comment: Tool-form community bundles: candidates for the image, tried in a throwaway profile first. A bundle registers model-facing tools and joins the host composition, so unlike a skill it cannot be taken piecemeal — either it is pinned into the image whole or it is not taken. `pnpm try:community-bundles` installs each into a scratch profile, boots it, and reports which ones survive. Nothing here is installed by the runtime image until it moves into the Dockerfile with an exact version.

candidates.name: dsh-cite
candidates.why: DOI/Crossref verification plus GB/T 7714 / APA / MLA / Chicago / BibTeX. GB/T 7714 is the format Chinese journals require and nothing we ship produces it.

candidates.name: dsh-plugin-academic-writing
candidates.why: Outline, title/abstract skeletons, citation formatting, submission checklist. Overlaps manuscript-support; worth measuring against it rather than assuming.

candidates.name: dsh-plugin-translation
candidates.why: Sentence splitting, glossary, and number/unit/parenthesis consistency checks — the mechanical half of bilingual manuscript work.

candidates.name: dsh-plugin-writing-guard
candidates.why: Deterministic, zero-network. Protects numbers, citations, claim strength, negation and scope from being changed by language polishing, and detects working-context residue leaking into deliverables — the same family as our own leakage bans, from the other side. Version 1.7.0 was never published; 2.0.1 is the first currently published candidate tested here. Reclassified from the skills lane because its SKILL.md calls its own tools, so the prose cannot be taken alone.

candidates.name: @changfenhuang/dsh-annotation
candidates.why: Select a passage in a reply, annotate it, send the annotations with the next message as plain text prepended to the user turn. The manuscript-review interaction we lack; the Node half is empty and nothing leaves the container. Risk to watch: its peer is the bare `cordis` package, not `@deepseek-ai/cordis`, which is the exact failure the two 2026-09-06 rejections had. Queued 2026-09-15.

candidates.name: dsh-mermaid
candidates.why: Client-only Mermaid renderer for fenced diagrams in replies (PRISMA flow, study-selection trees). No peers, no network. The counts in a diagram still have to come from the screening ledger, not be typed by the model. Queued 2026-09-15.

candidates.name: dsh-data-quality
candidates.why: Deterministic in-process profiling and, the part we lack, `data_verify`: numbers quoted in a document checked against a dataset snapshot with a tolerance and a four-value verdict. csv/tsv/json/jsonl only, so it complements rather than replaces `profile_dataset.py`. We do not `inject` its `dataQuality` service; only the model calls the tools. Queued 2026-09-15.

results.dsh-plugin-academic-writing@0.2.0: rejected: peer dependency does not admit the current DSH packages
results.dsh-plugin-translation@0.2.0: rejected: peer dependency does not admit the current DSH packages
results.dsh-plugin-writing-guard@2.0.1: rejected: dependency build scripts require an unreviewed pnpm approval

notInstalledYet: The three rejected bundles remain outside the runtime image. dsh-cite is pinned whole; its public tool builder uses the managed source gateway. Boot compatibility does not certify runtime connectivity, which requires cite_health and a successful DOI lookup with the current model token.
